rationale: The two solutions share the same from_pov/_reorient code, which in both cases mutates the original tree in place, so they differ only in path_to. B's recursive find is the textbook DFS shape: it appends the current node, checks whether this is the target, recurses into the children and backtracks. That covers the root case the same way as every other node. A seeds the path with the root, checks child labels inside the loop, and needs a separate `tree.label != to_node` guard for the root case, which splits one piece of logic across two places and is harder to read. B is slightly cleaner and more uniform.
